episode.title: Harden dangerous-command approval boundaries and preserve explicit bypass semantics
episode.before: At parent 3ab7e2aa9190c32abd8f854f9f6a88ad9a2c3d0e, both dangerous-command entry points reread HERMES_YOLO_MODE from mutable process environment state on every invocation, so in-process code could enable the process-wide bypass after startup. Smart approval accepted any normalized LLM response containing APPROVE or DENY as a substring. Remote-content detection only recognized curl/wget pipelines whose shell token was directly sh or bash. Dangerous commands automatically allowed outside interactive and gateway contexts produced no audit warning.
episode.after: At 4cb3eb03c750c902919906733b79220588ca5f16, process-wide YOLO configuration is parsed once at module import and both approval entry points consult the frozen value while retaining session-scoped bypass and existing hardline guards. Smart approval grants or denies only for exact normalized APPROVE or DENY tokens and escalates every other response. Remote-content detection additionally recognizes path-qualified sh/bash and bash -c forms. The legacy non-interactive, non-gateway auto-approval behavior remains, but each such approval emits a warning containing the matched description and a command prefix. YOLO tests patch the captured configuration value directly and continue checking bypass behavior in both approval entry points.
episode.diff: The commit modifies tools/approval.py and tests/tools/test_yolo_mode.py (20 insertions, 10 deletions). It adds one import-time boolean, replaces two runtime environment checks, tightens two LLM-response comparisons, broadens one dangerous-command regex, adds one warning before a legacy auto-approval return, and updates three tests to patch the module-level captured value instead of mutating HERMES_YOLO_MODE.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 4cb3eb03c750c902919906733b79220588ca5f16 resolves PR/issue 23835, has parent 3ab7e2aa9190c32abd8f854f9f6a88ad9a2c3d0e, and changes tools/approval.py plus tests/tools/test_yolo_mode.py.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json fields resolved_commit, parent_commit, linked_pull_requests, changed_files_name_status, and commit_show_stat; git show --stat 4cb3eb03c750c902919906733b79220588ca5f16

evidence_units.claim: The after state captures process-wide YOLO mode once during module import by parsing HERMES_YOLO_MODE into _YOLO_MODE_FROZEN.

The parent implementation read HERMES_YOLO_MODE at invocation time in both check_dangerous_command and check_all_command_guards; the change replaces both reads with _YOLO_MODE_FROZEN while retaining the session-scoped bypass and approval-mode branch.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3ab7e2aa9190c32abd8f854f9f6a88ad9a2c3d0e 4cb3eb03c750c902919906733b79220588ca5f16 -- tools/approval.py; after-state lines 946-949 and 1086-1090

evidence_units.claim: Smart approval normalizes the model response and now maps only exact APPROVE to approve and exact DENY to deny; all other content escalates, and exceptions also escalate.
The parent used substring tests for APPROVE and DENY, whereas the after state uses equality tests.
The remote-content pipeline rule recognizes curl or wget piped to sh/bash with an optional path prefix and permits a following whitespace, end-of-input, or -c suffix.
The parent pipeline rule only matched a directly named sh or bash token; the commit expands that single dangerous-command pattern.

When a dangerous command reaches the legacy non-interactive, non-gateway auto-approval branch, the after state logs a warning with the detection description and the first 200 command characters before returning approval.

Three YOLO tests now patch _YOLO_MODE_FROZEN directly and verify that recoverable dangerous commands remain approved through both the direct dangerous-command guard and the combined guard, with the combined guard avoiding downstream scanning.

Existing approval tests verify the exact APPROVE happy path and basic curl-to-sh detection, but the inspected commit does not add negative verbose-response cases, path-qualified shell cases, bash -c pipeline cases, or log-capture assertions.
evidence_units.source: git show 4cb3eb03c750c902919906733b79220588ca5f16:tests/tools/test_approval.py lines 34-46 and 63-80; git diff --name-status and patch for 4cb3eb03c750c902919906733b79220588ca5f16

evidence_units.claim: Terminal command execution delegates its consolidated pre-execution security decision to check_all_command_guards and supplies the CLI approval callback.
Hardline destructive-command checks and the unconditional sudo-stdin guard still execute before YOLO bypass evaluation, so the change does not broaden bypass authority over those guards.

candidate_atomics.name: capture_process_bypass_configuration
candidate_atomics.title: Capture process-wide bypass configuration at initialization
candidate_atomics.description: Convert startup-controlled bypass configuration into immutable runtime policy input so later in-process environment mutation cannot enable the process-wide approval bypass.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent untrusted or injected in-process behavior from escalating permissions by changing a process environment variable after the approval subsystem has initialized.
semantic_action.pre_state: Each approval check derives process-wide bypass authority from the current mutable environment.
semantic_action.post_state: Process-wide bypass authority is derived from a value captured during subsystem initialization; session-scoped bypass remains independently evaluated, and unconditional guards remain earlier in the decision order.
semantic_action.validation: Initialize with bypass enabled and disabled, mutate the environment afterward, and verify both approval entry points continue using the initialization-time value; also verify session-scoped bypass still works and hardline guards still block. The committed tests directly cover enabled frozen-state behavior but not post-import mutation resistance.

candidate_atomics.name: require_exact_policy_decision_token
candidate_atomics.title: Require an exact machine decision token
candidate_atomics.description: Treat auxiliary policy output as authoritative only when the normalized response exactly matches an allowed decision token; route verbose, ambiguous, or malformed output to escalation.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent incidental or adversarial decision words embedded in longer model output from granting or denying command execution.
semantic_action.pre_state: A response containing an approval or denial word anywhere in its normalized text is accepted as that decision.
semantic_action.post_state: Only exact normalized approval and denial tokens produce terminal decisions; every other response follows the conservative escalation path.
semantic_action.validation: Stub the policy model with exact APPROVE and DENY responses and with verbose, negated, multiple-token, empty, and exceptional responses; assert only exact tokens are accepted and all ambiguous/error cases escalate. The inspected suite covers only the exact APPROVE happy path.

candidate_atomics.name: cover_remote_shell_pipeline_variants
candidate_atomics.title: Detect path-qualified and argument-bearing remote shell pipelines
candidate_atomics.description: Broaden dangerous-command recognition so downloading remote content into a shell remains detectable when the shell is invoked through a path or with a command flag.

semantic_action.intent: Close syntax variants that allow remote content to be executed by a shell without matching the dangerous-command policy.
semantic_action.pre_state: The classifier recognizes curl/wget piped directly to sh or bash but misses supported path-qualified or bash -c spellings.
semantic_action.post_state: The classifier recognizes direct, path-qualified, and -c-suffixed sh/bash pipeline variants as remote-content shell execution.
semantic_action.validation: Run the classifier against curl and wget pipelines using sh, bash, /bin/bash, other path-qualified shell names, and bash -c, plus benign download-only commands; assert dangerous variants match and benign controls do not. The inspected suite directly covers only curl piped to sh and curl piped to bash.

candidate_atomics.name: audit_unattended_dangerous_auto_approval
candidate_atomics.title: Audit unattended dangerous-command auto-approvals
candidate_atomics.description: Preserve established unattended execution behavior while making every detected dangerous command that is automatically allowed visible in warning logs.

semantic_action.intent: Remove silent permission grants from unattended execution without changing whether legacy non-interactive commands execute.
semantic_action.pre_state: A detected dangerous command in a non-interactive, non-gateway context may be automatically approved without an audit event.
semantic_action.post_state: The same branch still approves the command, but emits a warning containing the matched policy description and a bounded command preview.
semantic_action.validation: Capture logs while checking a dangerous command in non-interactive, non-gateway, non-denying-cron context; assert approval is unchanged and exactly one warning contains the description and truncated preview. Also assert safe commands and blocked cron commands do not use this auto-approval warning. No dedicated log-capture regression test was added in the inspected commit.

candidate_atomics.name: align_tests_with_captured_configuration
candidate_atomics.title: Exercise bypass behavior through the captured policy state
candidate_atomics.description: Update bypass tests to control the newly captured configuration boundary directly and retain behavioral coverage of both approval entry points.

semantic_action.intent: Keep the test oracle aligned with initialization-time configuration semantics while preserving coverage of approved recoverable commands and combined-guard short-circuiting.
semantic_action.pre_state: Tests enable process-wide bypass by mutating the environment after the approval module has already been imported.
semantic_action.post_state: Tests set the captured policy value explicitly and verify bypass behavior through both direct and consolidated approval APIs.
semantic_action.validation: The YOLO tests assert approval of recoverable dangerous commands, null approval messages, coverage across multiple patterns, and avoidance of downstream combined-guard scanning when the captured flag is enabled.

candidate_workflows.name: harden_permission_bypass_and_decision_boundaries
candidate_workflows.title: Harden approval bypasses and unattended permission decisions
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for closing mutable-policy and parsing bypasses, expanding dangerous syntax coverage, preserving intentional unattended behavior with auditability, and reconciling tests with the revised configuration boundary.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure permission bypasses are established only from trusted lifecycle state, machine-generated decisions are accepted only under an exact contract, known dangerous syntax variants are classified, and unavoidable unattended grants are auditable without changing documented guard ordering.
when_to_use: A permission or approval subsystem rereads mutable process state when deciding whether to bypass checks.
An external or model-generated response is parsed into an allow/deny decision using substring or otherwise permissive matching.
Equivalent dangerous command spellings evade a syntax-based classifier.
An unattended compatibility path intentionally auto-approves detected dangerous operations but does so silently.
anti_goals: Do not move bypass checks ahead of unconditional catastrophic-command or credential guards.
Do not remove session-scoped bypass controls or convert them into process-global state.
Do not change legacy unattended auto-approval into blocking behavior as part of an audit-only hardening change.
Do not treat arbitrary explanatory model text as an authoritative permission decision.
Do not broaden command patterns without retaining benign control cases to detect false positives.
not_applicable_when: The bypass setting is intentionally mutable at runtime through an authenticated policy-management interface whose state transition is itself authorized and audited.
The decision producer and consumer already use a schema-validated structured protocol rather than free-form text.
Command execution is isolated in a context explicitly exempted from these host approval checks.
There is no implementation-bearing before/after state or no observable approval decision boundary.
inputs: Approval entry points and their guard ordering
Lifecycle of process-wide and session-scoped bypass state
Allowed policy-model decision vocabulary and conservative fallback
Dangerous-command syntax examples and benign controls
Interactive, gateway, cron, and unattended execution-context rules
Regression tests for direct and consolidated guard APIs
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one approval boundary can grant authority from mutable runtime state, permissively parsed external output, incomplete dangerous-syntax detection, or an unaudited unattended auto-approval branch.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Process-wide bypass state is fixed at initialization, session bypass remains scoped, unconditional guards retain precedence, external decisions require exact tokens, targeted dangerous syntax variants are detected, unattended grants emit bounded warnings, and tests address the revised configuration boundary.

steps.condition: Use when process-wide bypass authority is currently recomputed from mutable runtime configuration.
steps.validation: Compare both approval entry points and confirm they consume the same initialization-time flag after all unconditional guards.

steps.condition: Use when free-form external output is translated into an allow, deny, or escalation decision.
steps.validation: Exact allowed tokens map to their decisions; verbose, malformed, empty, and exceptional outputs take the conservative fallback.

steps.condition: Use when semantically equivalent path-qualified or argument-bearing remote-shell pipelines evade the classifier.
steps.validation: Representative direct, path-qualified, and -c pipeline variants match while benign download-only controls remain unmatched.

steps.condition: Use when policy intentionally preserves unattended auto-approval for compatibility.
steps.validation: Every detected dangerous command taking the unattended approval branch emits a bounded warning without changing the returned approval decision.

steps.condition: Always reconcile tests with the initialization boundary and validate all changed decision branches.
steps.validation: Direct and consolidated guards preserve intended bypass behavior; the full validation target should additionally cover post-initialization environment mutation, ambiguous model output, new pipeline spellings, and warning emission.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent/after diff to verify that both approval entry points share the captured bypass state and that unconditional guards still precede it.
Unit-test exact decision-token acceptance and conservative handling of all non-exact or failed responses.
Table-test newly supported dangerous syntax variants together with benign controls.
Capture warnings for the unattended dangerous-command branch and verify its legacy return value is unchanged.
Run direct-guard and consolidated-guard bypass tests, then run the broader approval test suite.
stop_conditions: Stop if lifecycle analysis cannot establish when trusted configuration is initialized relative to untrusted code execution.
Stop if changing bypass-state lifetime would break an authenticated runtime policy control rather than closing an unintended mutation path.
Stop if a broadened dangerous-command pattern produces unresolved benign false positives.
Stop if unattended behavior is not an intentional compatibility contract and requires a separate product decision about blocking.
Do not claim runtime validation complete when the required pinned checkout and test interpreter cannot be materialized.
unresolved_or_deferred: The commit does not add a regression test proving that post-import HERMES_YOLO_MODE mutation cannot enable bypass.
The commit does not add negative smart-approval tests for verbose or adversarial responses.
The commit does not add explicit tests for /bin/bash or bash -c remote-content pipelines.
The commit does not add a log-capture test for unattended auto-approval warnings.
Runtime execution of the pinned tests was unavailable in the supplied environment.

unresolved_questions: Whether CI outside the supplied evidence bundle executed and passed the relevant approval suites is unknown because status-check metadata is unavailable.
The intended handling of an exact ESCALATE token is inferred from the implementation's general fallback branch; no dedicated assertion was found in the inspected tests.
Runtime validation remains unavailable because the partial clone could not retrieve a missing object without network access and the attempted environment lacked a python executable.
